rationale: A job's first sold run (knownSoldListingIds.Count == 0, the same signal SearchPageService/MercariPriceBandCollector already use to decide whether known-sold pruning applies) now runs in 'backfill' mode instead of walking bands purely by count. Scrape:SoldBackfillDays (default 30, ScrapeOptions) sets a cutoff = now - N days, sourced from an injected TimeProvider (not DateTime.UtcNow) so tests can pin it with FakeTimeProvider. A new internal SoldBackfillPlanner (src/MarketMakerEtl.Core/Services/SoldBackfillPlanner.cs) owns the date-driven decision for one fetched band: it fetches the item page for a band's first and last listing (via the existing IScrapeClient + the Mercari IItemPageParser, matching the prototype's approach), resolves a sold date per listing (SoldDateParser.Parse(detail.SoldDate), falling back to the injected TimeProvider's current time when Status=='Sold' but no parsable date -- the 'trading, no lastSoldAt' case -- and to null, treated as in-window, when nothing is usable), and caches a tri-state DateLookup (Resolved(date-or-null) vs Unresolved) per listing id for the life of the run. Each item-page lookup retries up to 3 times (each attempt consuming its own unit of budget) on a thrown exception or a null parse result before giving up and caching Unresolved; a genuinely Unresolved item is treated as 'unknown' inside FindCutoff/ProbeMargin (it can only push the binary search's hi bound down, never lo, and is skipped rather than extending the in-window count in ProbeMargin), so a transient fetch failure at a binary-search midpoint can no longer push the stored cutoff later than it should be. Item-page lookups are capped by a new, dedicated Scrape:MaxBackfillItemPageFetches budget (ScrapeOptions, default 400) instead of sharing DetailFetchOptions.MaxDetailFetchesPerRun (the two budgets serve unrelated phases and the shared 50-fetch default was far too small for a 138-fetch backfill); once the budget is exhausted, ResolveDate returns Unresolved immediately (no further attempts), which -- combined with the tri-state FindCutoff/ProbeMargin fix -- makes the planner naturally stop guessing (an Unresolved oldest-item lookup can no longer trigger an incorrect Split) and store only what it had already conclusively resolved, rather than treating every not-yet-fetched item as in-window. A new SoldBackfillPlanner.BudgetExhausted flag surfaces this state; MercariPriceBandCollector threads it onto PriceBandCollectionSummary.BackfillBudgetExhausted, and SearchPageService (via the extracted SearchRunIssueFactory, split out of SearchPageService to stay under the CI0014 200-line-per-class limit) records a 'SoldBackfillBudgetExhausted' run issue when it fires. If the newest item is already older than the cutoff, the band contributes nothing. If the band's page is full (100 items) with a reported total over 100 and its last item is conclusively resolved as still inside the window, the band splits (its own items are not stored -- the children cover them) when it can still split, or is stored whole with an 'Overflowed' flag when it cannot split further (feeding the run issue in scope item 5). Otherwise a binary search over the page (using the already-resolved endpoints as the lo/hi anchors) finds the approximate cutoff position, then probes a fixed +/-3 position margin around it and takes one past the last in-window position seen in that margin -- tolerating the 2-3 local order inversions the prototype observed near real boundaries -- and only that many leading items are stored. MercariPriceBandCollector takes this planner through a new MercariCollectionSettings(int MaxBandsPerDirection, SoldBackfillPlanner? Backfill) record (replacing the old bare int parameter) to stay within the 5-constructor-parameter limit; when sold && knownSoldListingIds.Count == 0, SearchPageService builds a planner and passes it in, otherwise it passes null and the collector's existing count-based ShouldSplit/pruning path runs completely unchanged (AC-d). SearchPageService itself gained a MarketplaceAdapters(UrlServices, SearchParsers, ItemParsers) bundle replacing its two separate IEnumerable<...> constructor parameters, and dropped its now-unused DetailFetchOptions dependency in favor of a TimeProvider dependency (both changes keep it within the 5-parameter cap) so it can resolve the Mercari IItemPageParser and inject the clock needed to build the planner. PriceBandCollectionSummary gained ItemPageFetchesUsed / BackfillCutoffUtc / BandsOverCapacityUnsplit / BackfillBudgetExhausted fields (all default to 0/null/false so every pre-existing positional-construction call site in MercariPriceBandCollectorTests keeps compiling); SearchRunIssueFactory turns a non-null BackfillCutoffUtc into a 'SoldBackfillWindow' run issue, a positive BandsOverCapacityUnsplit into a 'SoldBackfillBandOverflow' run issue (scope item 5), and a true BackfillBudgetExhausted into a 'SoldBackfillBudgetExhausted' run issue, and SearchPageService threads ItemPageFetchesUsed through SearchCollectionResult -> ScrapeRunService -> RunCompletionCounts -> ScrapeRunEntity.BackfillItemPageFetches (new column, new migration) -> ScrapeRunView (scope item 4's 'record them on the run'). ItemDetailStore.GetListingsNeedingDetail now orders never-attempted sold listings before everything else (scope item 6, first half only -- the optional SoldDate write-through in scope item 6's second half is not implemented; see Gaps).
declaredRedTestsNote: Two tests originally declared before implementation were dropped as impractical/redundant during design: MercariPriceBandCollectorTests.Should_apply_backfill_only_to_the_sold_direction_of_a_jobs_first_run (superseded by Should_use_the_existing_incremental_pruning_path_when_the_job_already_has_sold_listings, which asserts the same branch more directly) and SearchPageServiceTests.Should_record_a_band_overflow_issue_when_a_backfill_band_cannot_split / MercariPriceBandCollectorTests.Should_record_bands_over_capacity_unsplit_on_the_summary (reaching an unsplittable band width requires ~9 sequential halvings of a seed band, disproportionate for this non-critical-path issue; the underlying Overflowed decision is instead covered directly at the planner level by SoldBackfillPlannerTests.Should_flag_overflow_when_a_full_in_window_band_cannot_split_further -- see AC-4's materialConcerns in criterion-checklist.json). SearchUsesTheMarketplaceImplementationTests.Should_use_the_url_builder_and_parser_of_the_requested_marketplace was not new work but needed a mechanical fix (registering the new MarketplaceAdapters/TimeProvider in its manual ServiceCollection) to keep passing after SearchPageService's constructor shape changed. A second, post-review round replaced SoldBackfillPlannerTests.Should_stop_fetching_item_pages_once_the_shared_detail_fetch_budget_is_exhausted with Should_store_only_what_is_already_decided_when_the_item_page_fetch_budget_is_exhausted: the old test asserted the pre-fix behavior (an exhausted budget causing the whole 3-item page to be stored, because every unresolved date was treated as in-window); the new test asserts the fixed, conservative behavior (only the one item whose date was actually resolved before the budget ran out is stored) against the new dedicated Scrape:MaxBackfillItemPageFetches budget. Should_resolve_the_date_after_the_item_page_fetch_fails_once_then_succeeds, Should_not_let_an_unresolvable_midpoint_push_the_cutoff_later, Should_compute_the_cutoff_from_the_injected_time_provider, Should_flag_the_backfill_budget_as_exhausted_when_item_page_fetches_run_out, and the two new MaxBackfillItemPageFetches config tests are new in that same round, driven directly by the reviewer's three numbered fix requests.
